medicines.name: Paracetamol (Acetaminophen)
medicines.instructions: Take after meals for fever and body aches. Do not exceed 3000 mg in 24 hours.
medicines.rationale: Primary fever and malaise relief; avoid Aspirin in viral infections.

medicines.name: Oseltamivir (Tamiflu)
medicines.instructions: Take with food to minimize GI upset. Complete full 5-day course.
medicines.rationale: FDA/WHO approved first-line antiviral against Influenza A and B within 48h.

medicines.name: Cetirizine Hydrochloride
medicines.instructions: For sneezing, rhinorrhea and nasal congestion. May cause mild drowsiness.
medicines.rationale: Symptomatic relief for upper respiratory allergic and viral secretions.

medicines.name: Dextromethorphan Hydrobromide
medicines.instructions: Sip for persistent dry cough. Do not exceed recommended dosage.
medicines.rationale: Centrally acting non-opioid suppressant for non-productive dry cough.

medicines.name: Acyclovir
medicines.instructions: Drink plenty of water. Complete full 7-day course to accelerate lesion crusting.
medicines.rationale: Significantly reduces vesicular lesion duration and systemic severity if started early.

medicines.name: Calamine + Zinc Oxide Lotion
medicines.instructions: Apply with cotton over itchy vesicular lesions. For external use only.
medicines.rationale: Soothes severe pruritus and prevents scratching-induced secondary bacterial infection.

medicines.name: Paracetamol
medicines.instructions: Take for fever and body ache. STRICTLY AVOID Aspirin and Ibuprofen.
medicines.rationale: Safe antipyretic; Aspirin is strictly contraindicated due to fatal Reye's syndrome risk.

medicines.name: Chlorpheniramine Maleate
medicines.instructions: Take at night to relieve intense nocturnal itching and promote restful sleep.
medicines.rationale: Prevents nocturnal excoriation of cutaneous vesicles.

medicines.name: Vitamin A (Retinol)
medicines.instructions: Administer orally immediately upon diagnosis under medical supervision.
medicines.rationale: WHO protocol: dramatically reduces measles-induced corneal damage, blindness, and mortality.

medicines.name: Paracetamol
medicines.instructions: Take for high fever and malaise. Maintain continuous oral fluid intake.
medicines.rationale: First-line antipyretic for high measles fever; safe profile.

medicines.name: Saline Nasal Drops
medicines.instructions: Clears thick nasal secretions and relieves upper airway obstruction.
medicines.rationale: Non-medicated gentle clearance for severe coryza and rhinitis.

medicines.name: Ibuprofen
medicines.instructions: Take with or after food. Provides potent anti-inflammatory relief for salivary gland pain.
medicines.rationale: NHS/CDC standard for reducing painful parotid salivary gland inflammation.

medicines.name: Paracetamol
medicines.instructions: Alternate with or use for persistent fever and headache.
medicines.rationale: Controls systemic fever without gastric irritation.

medicines.name: Warm / Cold Salivary Compress
medicines.frequency: Apply to jaw / swollen cheek 3 - 4 times daily
medicines.instructions: Apply gently over parotid swelling for 10-15 minutes to alleviate pain.
medicines.rationale: Non-pharmacological soothing of acute parotitis tension.

medicines.name: Hypromellose (Artificial Tears)
medicines.frequency: 1 - 2 drops into affected eye(s) 4 times daily
medicines.instructions: Wash hands before instilling. Avoid touching dropper tip to the eye.
medicines.rationale: CDC recommendation: provides symptomatic lubrication and washes away viral debris.

medicines.name: Olopatadine Hydrochloride
medicines.frequency: 1 drop in each affected eye BD (every 12 hrs)
medicines.instructions: Provides fast relief for itching, redness and conjunctival edema.
medicines.rationale: High patient satisfaction in drug reviews (7.1/10 rating) for ocular irritation.

medicines.name: Cold Ocular Compress
medicines.frequency: Apply over closed eyelids 3 times daily for 10 mins
medicines.instructions: Soothes burning sensation and eyelid swelling. Do not share cloths.
medicines.rationale: Vasoconstricts dilated conjunctival vessels and relieves burning.

medicines.name: Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS Low-Osmolarity)
medicines.frequency: 200 - 300 ml after each loose stool / vomit
medicines.instructions: Sip slowly. Primary medical intervention to replace lost electrolytes and fluids.
medicines.rationale: WHO/UNICEF gold standard: prevents dehydration shock and electrolyte disturbance.

medicines.name: Zinc Sulfate
medicines.instructions: Take with meals. Continue full 10-14 days even after diarrhea resolves.
medicines.rationale: Significantly shortens viral diarrhea duration and regenerates intestinal mucosa.

medicines.name: Ondansetron
medicines.frequency: 1 Tablet BD PRN for active vomiting
medicines.instructions: Dissolve on tongue 30 mins before rehydration drinks if experiencing intractable vomiting.
medicines.rationale: Rated 9.4/10 in drug reviews; controls intractable nausea to facilitate oral rehydration.

medicines.name: Paracetamol
medicines.frequency: 1 Tablet TDS PRN for abdominal cramps or fever
medicines.instructions: Take with sips of water. Avoid NSAIDs due to gastric mucosal irritation.
medicines.rationale: Safe antipyretic without gastric ulceration risk.
